content:
In the Carleson project, we are in cleaning up the HardyLittlewood file and its dependencies to upstream them to Mathlib. Currently, the uncentered maximal function is defined over an arbitrary family of balls in a PseudoMetricSpace (represented as two functions c : ι → X and r : ι → ℝ), for which it is shown to have strong/weak type. Then the uncentered maximal function is the specialization of this generalized form to the family of all open balls.

This was originally written this way due to a particularity of the proof that was then removed, and due to some other needs in the project. But it would be possible to save some lines of code on the upstreamed version by removing this generalized form and have only the definition considering all open balls.

The question is, is there motivation for having the generalized form of the uncentered maximal function in Mathlib? Perhaps there are areas for which choosing the family of open balls would be desirable?

(as a note, the centered version is not a specialization of this generalized form)
